edition_notes: Helvetiq; game design Cédric Martinez, illustration Emiliano Ponzi; trilingual rulebook (English/French/German); 1–7 players, 10+, 30 min; optional free companion app can act as Savvy

items.rule: One player is chosen to be Savvy (the lab computer / game master); the remaining players split into 2 teams (Lab-T and Lab-M) of 1 to 3 players each. The free app can replace Savvy.
The two teams sit on opposite sides of the table facing each other, each hiding their material behind their screen.
Each team takes its lab components: 1 screen, 1 Tool Cards deck, 1 Sample Cards deck, 1 Scanpad, 1 Centrifugo, 1 Estugamo, 1 Research sheet, 1 pencil.
Each team writes its team name and player names on the Research sheet, which shows 25 numbered molecules surrounded by lab tools.
For beginners, only use these tools: Dedukto, Samply, Analyzer, Scanpad, Intervallo, Antidote; all other tool cards go back in the box.
Each team shuffles its Sample Cards deck and places its Tool Cards faceup in front of it, sorted by type.

Savvy randomly draws 3 cards from the Molecule Cards deck, memorizes them (the secret antidote molecules) and sets them aside hidden from both teams; the remaining Molecule Cards form a facedown deck between the teams.
At the start of each round, each team freely chooses one Tool Card from its available cards and passes it facedown to Savvy.
When both teams have chosen, Savvy reveals the tools; then each lab applies its tool with Savvy's help.
The team that selected its tool first plays first; a lab cannot proceed to the next round until the other lab finishes applying its tool for the round.
Each Tool Card can only be played once, but a team may have several cards for the same tool (number of copies per lab shown per tool). Used Tool Cards stay faceup and visible to everyone.
Teams should discuss discreetly (whispering) so the opponents don't benefit; bluffing is allowed.

Samply (3x per lab): draw 3 cards from the top of your Sample deck and give them to Savvy, who places them on the right (✔) side of the sheet if the card contains at least one secret molecule, on the left (✘) side if none. You may look at them anytime.

Mikroskopo (3x): the team has one minute to look through the whole Sample deck and choose 2 Sample Cards for Savvy, who sorts them ✔/✘ as with Samply; then shuffle the Sample deck. (Not in beginner set.)
Dedukto (1x): receive 5 Molecule Cards from Savvy that contain none of the secret molecules; keep them hidden behind your screen.

Analyzer (3x): usable only if Samply or Mikroskopo was used before; give up to 3 cards from the ✔ side to Savvy, who returns them to the x1, x2 or x3 slot according to how many secret molecules (1, 2, 3) the card contains.
Intervallo (1x): choose Min or Max; Savvy marks the row of the Research sheet containing the secret molecule with the lowest (Min) or highest (Max) number.
Scanpad (1x): place the Scanpad over 6 molecules (vertically or horizontally); Savvy marks how many of them (0 to 3) are part of the solution.

Other tools outside the beginner set: Centrifugo (4 molecules, at least one secret?), Estugamo (row or column of 5, at least one secret?), Hackz (copy the opponent's tool, they also play it), Spionado (see 2 cards from opponent's ✘ side), Fuzio (sum zone of the 3 secret numbers), Substrakto (difference of 2 random secret molecules, 2x), Kolozomi (needs Dedukto; color match, 2x), Mezakol (color of the middle secret molecule).
Antidote (2x per lab): circle the 3 molecules you think form the antidote; Savvy checks a box on the Antidote section (0 to 3 correct). A 3 wins the game; otherwise the team gets one more chance.
A team that fails to find the antidote with its second Antidote card loses, and the other team keeps searching for the antidote.
The game ends as soon as a team plays the Antidote tool and correctly identifies all 3 secret molecules. A game typically lasts 6 to 8 rounds.

There are no points in the standard game; the goal is to find the antidote first. Optionally in solo/Lean mode, rate performance by number of Tool Cards used: 4 or fewer = 2 Nobel prizes; 5 = Nobel potential; 6 = world-acclaimed; 7 = tenured professors; 8 = excellent researchers; 9 = up and coming lab technicians; 10 or more = promising students.
The first team to find the antidote (3 correct molecules) wins; also a team wins if the opponent has used up both Antidote cards without success and it itself finds the antidote.
Ties are not possible, so no tie-break is needed.

No Savvy mode (2+ players): each lab draws 3 Molecule Cards for the opposing team to find, each team acts as Savvy for the other; remove the Spionado tool; when playing Dedukto, the Savvy side must not see the Molecule Cards given.
Lean mode (1–2 players): one lab plus Savvy (a player or the app); goal is to find the antidote with the fewest Tool Cards played, rated on the 'How good were you?' scale.
Agile mode (1–7 players): for each lab randomly remove 10 Tool Cards from the deck, making sure the 2 Antidote cards remain.

Disruption mode (1–7 players): shuffle the Disruption deck facedown in front of Savvy; after each lab has played 3 tools, Savvy draws a disruption card whose effect applies to both labs for the rest of the game.
